title: Any client can read every customer's contact, ID-number and card details through /admin/customers
summary: GET /admin/customers returns 200 with all customer records to client accounts from three different companies; the spec and business rules say only admins may see customers.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 (client)
GET /api/admin/customers (see evidence for the exact request)
Observe HTTP 200 with records for all three companies, including fields for phone, national ID, address and card digits
Repeat as zain-1 (client of another company): same result
expected: HTTP 403 for non-admin roles (matches /admin/reports/sales, which does return 403)
actual: HTTP 200 with the full customer list including personal and card-related fields
suspected_cause: The customers route is missing the admin role check that the reports route has

regression_test.description: As a client, GET /admin/customers and expect 403 with no body data

title: A client can open another company's order by id (cross-customer data exposure)
summary: GET /orders/{id} returns the full order (items, company name, totals) to clients of other companies; the list endpoint is correctly scoped, but the detail endpoint is not.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 and POST /api/orders with reference QA-iso-1, capture the id
Sign in as bright-1 (Bright Foods) and GET /api/orders/{id}
Observe HTTP 200 containing the Acme order
Repeat as zain-1: same result
UI: signed in as zain-1 in the Client Portal, open /order.html?id=o-1036 and see Acme Traders' order QA-ui-1 (screenshot)
expected: HTTP 403 or 404 and no order data
actual: HTTP 200 with the other company's order, in the API and in the Client Portal
suspected_cause: Order lookup by id does not filter on the caller's client_id

regression_test.description: Client A creates an order; client B GETs it by id and expects 403/404; A re-reads it

title: Signing out does not revoke the token: the same token still works afterwards
summary: After POST /auth/logout returns 204, the same bearer token still gets 200 from GET /me. The spec and business rules say sign-out ends the session at once.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-2
POST /api/auth/logout with that token: HTTP 204
GET /api/me with the same token
Observe HTTP 200 with the user's profile
suspected_cause: Logout does not add the token to a revocation list (or the check ignores it)

regression_test.description: Login, logout, then GET /me with the same token expects 401

title: Tax is calculated on the pre-discount subtotal, so discounted orders are overcharged
summary: For orders at or above 1,000.00 the 10% tax is applied to the undiscounted subtotal instead of the discounted one, so totals are too high. Below the threshold the maths is correct.
steps: Sign in as acme-1; POST /api/orders with 100 x p-101 and 100 x p-104 (subtotal 1000.00)
Observe discount_cents 5000, tax_cents 10000, total_cents 105000; expected tax 9500 and total 104500
Repeat with 1000 x p-101: tax 65000, total 682500; expected tax 61750 and total 679250
UI: place 200 x A4 Copy Paper in the Client Portal; confirmation says $1,365.00, expected $1,358.50 (1300.00 - 65.00 + 123.50)
actual: Tax is 10% of the full subtotal (e.g. 130.00 instead of 123.50 on a 1,300.00 order); shown identically in the UI, the list, the order detail and the admin portal
suspected_cause: Tax computed from subtotal_cents rather than subtotal_cents - discount_cents

regression_test.description: Order at 1000.00 expects discount 5000, tax 9500, total 104500; also 999.50 and 1004.75

title: Order quantity is not validated: 0, negative, above 1000 and fractional quantities are accepted
summary: POST /orders returns 201 for quantity 0, -1, 1001 and 1.5, contradicting the 1 to 1000 whole-number rule; a quantity of -1 creates an order with a negative total that appears in lists and reports.
steps: Sign in as acme-1
POST /api/orders with items[0].quantity = -1 (QA- reference)
Observe HTTP 201 and total_cents -715
Repeat with quantity 0, 1001 and 1.5: all HTTP 201
actual: HTTP 201; negative-total orders are stored and counted in the admin sales report
suspected_cause: No range or integer check on item quantity

regression_test.description: POST orders with quantity -1, 0, 1001, 1.5 expect 400; 1 and 1000 expect 201

title: An order with no items is accepted
summary: POST /orders with an empty items array returns 201; the rules require at least one item.
steps: Sign in as acme-1
POST /api/orders with items: [] (see evidence)
Observe HTTP 201

regression_test.description: POST order with empty items expects 400

title: Order list shows stale status after an admin changes it
summary: After an admin moves an order forward, the client's order detail updates at once but the client's order list keeps showing the old status for a while (warm, change, re-read).
steps: Sign in as acme-1; GET /api/orders?q=QA-iso-1 and GET the order (status placed)
As admin, PATCH /api/admin/orders/{id}/status to processing
As acme-1 GET the order: processing; GET /api/orders?q=QA-iso-1: still placed
UI: the Client Portal My orders page showed Placed for an order that was already Delivered; a later fresh load showed Delivered
expected: List and detail show the new status immediately
actual: List served stale data (roughly a minute or more observed in the UI); detail and list disagree
suspected_cause: A cache on the client order list is not invalidated by status changes

regression_test.description: Warm list, change status as admin, re-read list and expect the new status

title: GET /orders returns HTTP 500 for page_size=0 and for q containing ( or \
summary: Invalid or special-character query values crash the list endpoint with a 500 instead of a 400 or a plain search. Separately, page_size=-1 returns 200 although the spec minimum is 1 (and page_size=101 correctly returns 400).
steps: Sign in as acme-1 (admin behaves the same)
GET /api/orders?page_size=0 : HTTP 500
GET /api/orders?q=( : HTTP 500
GET /api/orders?q=\ : HTTP 500
GET /api/orders?page_size=-1 : HTTP 200
expected: 400 for page_size below 1; special characters searched literally
actual: HTTP 500 for three inputs; HTTP 200 for page_size=-1
suspected_cause: Search text is used as a raw regular expression; page_size is not range-checked at the low end

regression_test.description: GET /orders with page_size=0/-1 expects 400; q='(' and q='\' expect 200

title: Malformed JSON responses include a stack trace and server file paths
summary: Sending invalid JSON to POST /auth/login or POST /orders returns a 400 whose body includes a trace field with a stack trace and absolute file paths; the spec says responses never include server internals.
steps: POST /api/auth/login (no token needed) with the raw body {"broken":
Observe HTTP 400 with error.trace containing file paths and function names
Repeat on POST /api/orders as acme-1: same
expected: A short error with code and message only
actual: error.trace holds a stack trace and local file system paths
suspected_cause: The JSON-parse error handler serialises the Error stack into the response

regression_test.description: Send malformed JSON and assert the body has no trace/stack and no file paths

title: Submitting the same order twice at once creates two orders
summary: Two identical POST /orders requests sent in parallel both return 201, so one user action can place a duplicate order. I am not sure whether the product intends to allow identical orders; there is no idempotency key or duplicate warning.
steps: Sign in as acme-1
Send the same POST /api/orders (reference QA-...) twice at the same moment
Observe two 201 responses with different order ids
expected: One order, or a clear duplicate refusal/warning
suspected_cause: No de-duplication on reference and no idempotency support

regression_test.description: Parallel identical POSTs yield one order or a 409

title: Sales report endpoint takes about 4 seconds to respond
summary: GET /admin/reports/sales consistently takes about 4 seconds with only a few dozen orders, and the Reports page waits just as long.
steps: Sign in as admin
GET /api/admin/reports/sales
Observe a response time of 4001 to 4009 ms, repeated in every run
expected: Under about 3 seconds for a small data set
suspected_cause: Artificial delay or an unoptimised aggregation

regression_test.description: Report responds in under 3000 ms with the seeded data

title: New order page is wider than the screen on mobile; Place order button is off-screen
summary: At 390px the form is 555px wide: the page scrolls sideways, the Place order, Quantity and Remove controls sit past the right edge, and Remove is covered by the Quantity field.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1 with a 390x844 viewport
Open New order (/new-order.html)
Observe horizontal scrolling (scroll width 555) and the Place order button starting at x=435
Reload and repeat: same
expected: Form fits the screen and all controls are reachable
actual: Controls pushed off-screen; a user must scroll sideways to place an order
suspected_cause: Fixed-width line-item row with no wrapping at narrow widths

regression_test.description: At 390px the New order page does not scroll sideways and Place order is within the viewport

title: My orders table cuts off the Total column on mobile with no cue
summary: At 390px the table scrolls inside its own box; the Total column is clipped and the Date wraps to three lines, and the first row sits partly under the filter bar.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 with a 390x844 viewport
Open My orders
Observe the clipped Total column and a row overlapped by the toolbar
Reload: same
expected: Totals visible without hidden horizontal scrolling
suspected_cause: Table wider than the viewport inside an overflow container

regression_test.description: At 390px the Total column is visible on My orders

title: Form controls without accessible names (product select, search, icon buttons)
summary: The product dropdown on New order, the Admin Orders search box (placeholder only) and the two icon buttons (refresh, clear filters) have no accessible name, so screen readers cannot announce them.
steps: Open the Client Portal New order page and run the page audit: unnamed select[name=product]
Open the Admin Portal Orders page and run the audit: unnamed search input, refresh and clear-filters buttons
Repeat at mobile width: same
expected: Every control has a label or aria-label

regression_test.description: Accessibility check asserts every form control has an accessible name on these pages

title: Urdu order references render with the hyphen on the wrong side in a left-to-right cell
summary: Urdu references such as the company-prefix plus number are placed in left-to-right, left-aligned cells without dir handling, so the hyphen and number order look scrambled.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as zain-1
Open My orders
Look at the three Urdu references: the hyphen appears at the start of the word and the number follows (see screenshot)
The audit flags the same three cells as RTL text in an LTR container
expected: Mixed Urdu-and-number text displayed in a readable order (dir=auto or bdi)
suspected_cause: No dir="auto" or <bdi> on user-provided text

regression_test.description: Render an Urdu reference and assert dir=auto on the cell
